result.markdown: --- title: "Plotting & Maps" --- ## Basic Plotting with Plots.jl ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Plots x = 0:0.1:2π y = sin.(x) plot(x, y, label="sin(x)", xlabel="x", ylabel="y", lw=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ### Multiple Series ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} plot(x, sin.(x), label="sin(x)", lw=2) plot!(x, cos.(x), label="cos(x)", lw=2, ls=:dash) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ### Scatter Plots ::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} x = randn(50) y = randn(50) scatter(x, y, xlabel="X", ylabel="Y", title="Random Points", markersize=5, alpha=0.7) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ### Heatmaps ::: {#8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} z = [sin(x) * cos(y) for x in 0:0.1:2π, y in 0:0.1:2π] heatmap(z, xlabel="X", ylabel="Y", title="2D Function", color=:viridis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ## Subplots ::: {#10 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} p1 = plot(x, sin.(x), title="Sine") p2 = plot(x, cos.(x), title="Cosine") p3 = plot(x, tan.(x), title="Tangent", ylims=(-5, 5)) p4 = scatter(randn(20), randn(20), title="Random") plot(p1, p2, p3, p4, layout=(2, 2), size=(700, 500)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ## Contour Plots ::: {#12 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} x = -2:0.1:2 y = -2:0.1:2 z = [exp(-(xi^2 + yi^2)) for xi in x, yi in y] contour(x, y, z', levels=10, fill=true, xlabel="X", ylabel="Y", title="Gaussian") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: ## Geographic Maps ::: {.callout-note} ## Under Construction Geographic mapping examples with GeoMakie.jl and GMT.jl will be added soon. ::: ### Coordinate Systems ::: {#14 .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # Example with projected coordinates using CoordinateTransformations using Proj4 # Transform from WGS84 to UTM wgs84 = Proj4.Projection("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84") utm35 = Proj4.Projection("+proj=utm +zone=35 +datum=WGS84") ``` ::: ### Plotting Geophysical Data ::: {#16 .cell execution_count=0} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # Gravity anomaly map example using Plots # Create synthetic gravity data nx, ny = 50, 50 x = range(0, 10, length=nx) y = range(0, 10, length=ny) gz = [10 * exp(-((xi-5)^2 + (yi-5)^2)/2) for xi in x, yi in y] heatmap(x, y, gz', xlabel="Easting (km)", ylabel="Northing (km)", title="Bouguer Gravity Anomaly", colorbar_title="mGal", color=:RdBu) ``` :::
